title: Timeline: gesture zoom, and a drop makes the track it needs — web and desktop (#765, #771)
body:
## What changed

**Core (`crates/core`)**
- `TrackKind::taking(AssetKind) -> Option<TrackKind>`: the one statement of which lane an asset kind sits on (`is_visual` → video, `is_audible` → audio). `check_reference` now reads it, so validation and "which lane do I make" cannot drift. Behaviour-preserving: the two predicates are disjoint and cover every kind (a test enumerates all 14, `html` included).
- `placing::place_on_new_track(project, asset, start, duration) -> (TrackId, Clip)`: makes a lane the way `track_new` does (`authoring::numbered`, appended — a new video track goes on top) and places the clip on it via `place`, **all or nothing** — a refused clip leaves no empty lane. New `PlaceError::NoTrackKind` for a future kind that belongs on neither track (unreachable today). `place` and `place_clip`'s contract are untouched: naming a missing track is still refused.

**Desktop (`app/src/timeline/drop/`)** — #771
- A drop goes on the lane under the pointer when that lane takes the asset's kind; on a lane of the other kind, below the last lane, or on an empty timeline it calls `place_on_new_track`.
- The ghost no longer shows the wrong-kind refusal; it previews the new lane **where it will be**, read from the placed project's own layout (so a new video lane is previewed above the audio block, a new audio lane at the bottom).
- `drop.rs` became `drop/mod.rs` + `drop/tests.rs` (size gate).

**Web (`web/src/editor/`)** — #765 + #771
- Pinch / Ctrl+wheel zoom (`timeline/zoom.ts`): multiplicative, clamped to the old 10–320 px/s range, keeping the time under the pointer fixed; a native non-passive `wheel` listener so `preventDefault` stops the page zoom; plain wheel still scrolls. A mouse notch (pixels or Firefox lines) is capped so it zooms as much as a short pinch.
- The toolbar strip (− / + zoom, "+ Video track" / "+ Audio track") is gone.
- `timeline/NewLane.tsx`: the space below the last lane (the whole timeline when empty) is a drop target. While an asset is being dragged anywhere on the page it shows a dashed "Drop here for a new track" and lights up under the pointer; on an empty timeline it reads "Drag something here from the left."
- `drop.ts`: `dropOnto` places on the lane when it takes the kind, otherwise `track_new {kind}` then `place_clip` on the lane that appeared. If `place_clip` is refused the new empty lane stays and the refusal shows, as #765 specifies.
- i18n: `videoTrack`, `audioTrack`, `zoom`, `zoomOut`, `zoomIn` removed; `empty` reworded and `newTrack` added — in en, pt-BR and es, kept together under `editor.timeline`.

## Why
The maintainer, 2026-10-05: having to click "audio track" before dragging a sound is not intuitive. Knowing a sound needs an audio lane is expert knowledge the north star says nobody should need; Filmora 9 just makes the track. Gesture zoom is what every editor does and frees the toolbar. Both surfaces in one branch, because the app is the product and the web follows it.

## Decisions
- **Shared core function: yes for Rust, no new tool for the web.** The desktop calls `place_on_new_track`. The web makes two existing tool calls (`track_new`, `place_clip`) rather than a new atomic tool or an optional `track` on `place_clip` — changing the tool surface is a design decision, and the batch brief said to reuse the existing track-creation path. The web's kind mapping (`laneFor`, already there) is TypeScript and can't call core; its doc now points at `TrackKind::taking`. Consequence: on the web a refused placement leaves an empty lane (as #765 accepted); on desktop it doesn't.
- **Below the last lane always makes a new lane**, even when a lane of the right kind exists above — that's what the space is for (#765). Gaps between lanes on desktop stay inert, as before.
- **No new desktop hint text**: the desktop ghost previewing the new lane is its hint; the desktop app wasn't in #765's scope.
- The assets sidebar's empty text ("…drag them onto a track") is left alone — the sidebar is #764/#770's.

## Effect
Dropping anything anywhere on either timeline works; nobody makes a track first. Web timeline zooms by gesture.

## Gates
On head `824f92f` (rebased on `origin/main` 2303387): `format`, `size`, `clippy`, `docs`, `test` (3318/3318, Postgres included), `scripts`, `deny`, `deploy`, `app` (panel snapshots unchanged), `web` (lint, typecheck, 134 tests, build) — all green. Mutation signal on the core diff (`cargo mutants --in-diff`): 6 mutants, 3 caught, 3 unviable, no survivors. No new dependency; no schema or `SYNTH_VERSION` change.

## Human checklist
- [ ] Web, trackpad: pinch zooms the timeline (not the page), centred on the pointer; two-finger scroll still scrolls.
- [ ] Web, mouse: Ctrl+wheel zooms around the pointer in steady steps; plain wheel scrolls.
- [ ] Web: on a new project, dragging an asset over the timeline shows the dashed hint; dropping makes a lane of the right kind with the clip on it.
- [ ] Web: a sound dropped on a video lane, and a picture below the last lane, each make a new lane with the clip at the drop point.
- [ ] Desktop: the same three drops (empty timeline, below the last lane, sound on a video lane) make the lane, and the ghost shows it where it appears before letting go.
- [ ] Desktop: dropping onto an existing clip still shows the alert colour and the reason.

Closes #765
Closes #771

title: Pin one chrome-headless-shell build, with a verified fetch script (#772)
body:
## What changed

- **`tools/chromium/pin`**: the one `chrome-headless-shell` build scorsese renders `html` clips with. It holds version **154.0.8037.92**, the Chrome for Testing URL pattern (`{version}`/`{platform}` placeholders), and a sha256 for each supported platform's zip (linux64, mac-arm64, mac-x64, win64), each computed from the downloaded file. Each entry is a plain `KEY=value` line, so a shell can `.`-source it and Rust can `include_str!` it and split on the first `=`. Both readers share that format, so there's only ever one copy of the version.
- **`tools/chromium/fetch`**: downloads the pinned zip for this platform and **refuses it if the sha256 differs**. It unpacks the zip beside the target and moves it into place in one step, then prints the binary's path, and only that, on stdout. The install goes to `<dir>/<version>/chrome-headless-shell-<platform>/`, where `<dir>` is the argument or `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/scorsese/chromium`. A stamp records which checksum was verified, so a re-run downloads nothing, and a pin that changes a checksum without changing the version still re-downloads. Its header shows the `actions/cache` + `$GITHUB_ENV` snippet #775 will paste into `ci.yml`.

## Why

#594 settled on one pinned Chromium + SwiftShader so that app, web and CI pixels are the same pixels. #775's goldens, #776's first-use download and #778's web image all need the same build, and two copies of a version number drift.

## The measurement (#772's question)

**CI reproduces the frames.** A GitHub `ubuntu-24.04` runner (AMD EPYC 7763, no AVX-512) and a cloud container (Intel Xeon, AVX-512) produced **byte-identical** RGBA for every feature of #606's sample page, on SwiftShader and on software raster. The one exception is a rare SwiftShader race on one frame: 6 pixels, one level each, SSIM 0.9999. It also happens on each machine against itself, so it isn't CPU-dependent. So #775 can bless `html` goldens on any x86_64 Linux and check them on CI with `crates/golden`'s existing tolerance, but it shouldn't assert bytes. The full table and method are on #772 ([results](https://github.com/MatthewLacerda2/scorsese/issues/772#issuecomment-6002243868), [reading](https://github.com/MatthewLacerda2/scorsese/issues/772#issuecomment-6002254890)), and there's a summary on #594.

## Decisions

- **No Chromium fetch step in `ci.yml` in this PR** (orchestrator, 2026-10-05). Nothing uses Chromium in CI until #775's first golden, so the step would cost every CI run for nothing. This PR lands the pin and a reusable fetch script. #775 calls the script from `ci.yml` (cached on `hashFiles('tools/chromium/pin')`), and #776's Rust download and #778's Docker image read the same pin. That is the shape of #772's deliverable 2, so this PR closes it.
- **Version 154.0.8037.92, the build #606 measured**, rather than "today's Stable". Every speed, memory and determinism figure in #606, and now #772's CI comparison, is for this build. Moving it means re-measuring. It's also only two days old, and this container can't reach the CfT version index (`googlechromelabs.github.io` is blocked by the egress proxy; the `storage.googleapis.com` downloads are not).
- **The comparison was cloud container vs CI runner**, not vs the maintainer's machine, whose frames aren't reachable (orchestrator). Both are x86_64 Linux on different CPUs, which is exactly the golden situation.
- **No `SCORSESE_CHROME` export in the script itself.** It prints a path and the caller names the variable. #775 owns that name (its discovery mirrors `tools::FFMPEG_ENV`).

## Effect

No Rust, no CI change, no behaviour change. Two new files under `tools/chromium/`.

## Left for a human

- [ ] **Delete the throwaway branch `772-measure`** (`git push origin --delete 772-measure`). This session's proxy refuses branch deletion through git and the API. It's inert: its only workflow fires on pushes to itself. It never becomes a PR.
- [ ] (optional) Run `tools/chromium/fetch` once on the Mac to see the mac-arm64 checksum verify on real hardware. All four checksums were computed from fresh downloads, but only linux64 has been through the script.

## Gates

`make gates` all green on `b59e0cb` (= this head, rebased on `origin/main` 52571fd): format, size, scripts, clippy, docs, test, deny, deploy. web and app were not run (the branch touches neither). `shellcheck tools/chromium/fetch` is clean apart from SC1091 (info: it doesn't follow the sourced pin without `-x`). The fetch script was tested here on a fresh download (6 s), a cached re-run (0.02 s, no download), and a tampered checksum (refused, exit 1, previous install untouched).

Closes #772

title: Assistant asks a question mid-edit and resumes the same turn (#710)
body:
Closes #710

## What changed

The web assistant can stop halfway through an edit, ask the user **one short question with 2–4 options plus a free-text field**, and carry on **in the same turn** with the answer.

**Server (`crates/server/src/assistant`)**
- `ask/mod.rs` — the `ask_user` function: its declaration (`{question, options}`, JSON Schema with `minItems: 2`, `maxItems: 4`, every argument described), its validation, and the result the model gets. The loop appends it **after** the registry's tools in `turn.rs`, so it's part of the constant cached prefix. It is **never** in `crate::tools` or `scorsese_mcp::registry()`, so web MCP never lists it (tested in `tests/mcp/described.rs`).
- `turn.rs` — when a reply's only call is a well-formed `ask_user`, the turn ends its loop as `End::Asking(question)` and `settle` pauses it rather than finishing it. If the model calls `ask_user` **beside** other tools, those tools run and `ask_user` gets an error result telling it to ask alone. That way a pause never splits tool results that have to go back together in one user message. A Stop requested during the call that asks wins over pausing. `Running` gained `spent`, so the per-turn cap covers the calls made before and after the question.
- `ask/answer.rs` — `answer` resumes the paused turn in one transaction. It replays the earlier turns, takes this turn's own kept bytes and record, appends the `ask_user` result (`The person answered: …`) frozen in the turn's model's wire, sets the state back to `running`, records the answer on the question, and spawns `turn::run` again. It refuses the same way a new message would: `402` with no credit, `503` with no key. In that case the question keeps waiting. `set_aside` handles Stop on a paused turn.
- `start.rs` — if the conversation's last turn is `asking`, a new chat message **is the answer**: the same turn resumes and no new turn is created. A new conversation (`fresh`) sets any waiting question aside.
- `quote.rs` — a quote can't be answered while a question waits (`400`, "answer it first"); a running turn is still `409`.
- `store/asking.rs` + migration **`0021_assistant_questions.sql`** — adds a new `asking` state to the `chat_turns_state_check` constraint, plus `questions JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'`: the cards the panel draws (`{question, options, answer}`), in order.
- `prompt.rs` — the system prompt says when to ask: only when the answer changes what happens next and the request points to no default. Never to confirm a step, and never about money.
- `http` — `POST /api/chat/turns/{id}/answer` `{answer}` → `202` with the same turn. Stop on an `asking` turn ends it at once as `stopped`.

**Web (`web/src/editor/chat`)**
- `QuestionCard.tsx`, shown inside the turn: option buttons, an "own words" field, and after answering the question with its answer.
- The composer stays open while a question waits; its placeholder says a message sent now is the answer, and Stop sets the question aside. A paused turn's cost line reads "so far; nothing more while it waits".
- `TurnView.questions` and the `asking` state were added to `api/chat.ts`; helpers `asking` / `waitingQuestion` / `typedAnswer` are tested in `question.test.ts`.

**Docs** — `docs/web.md` covers the flow, the route, the stop/quote interactions and the `TurnView.questions` shape.

## Why

The decisions are the issue's. Before this, an answer to a mid-edit question started a fresh turn that had to rebuild where the edit was. Now the model carries on with its plan, its thinking blocks and its prompt cache intact.

## Effect

- **History stays append-only and byte-exact.** The resumed call's messages begin with exactly the bytes the paused call was sent, plus the reply that asked (thinking block included) and then the result. Tested on Claude (`asking::resumes::a_question_pauses_the_turn_free_and_the_answer_resumes_it`) and on Gemini (`on_gemini_a_typed_message_is_the_answer`, which checks for a `functionResponse` named `ask_user`).
- **Nothing is charged while it waits.** The test checks no further model request is made and `charged_micros` stays at one call. After the answer, the resumed call is charged and gets its own `model_calls` row in the charge transaction (#707): two rows for the turn.

## Decisions

- **A waiting question does not expire.** A paused turn holds no process, no money and no quote token, and it survives a server restart unchanged (`recover` only touches `running`). A late answer costs at most one uncached call, the same as any late reply, so a deadline would protect nothing. What ends an unanswered question is the user: Stop, or a new conversation. This is also written in `ask/mod.rs`.
- **Migration 0021 rather than reusing a column.** #742 avoided a migration by recording a change as `declined`. Here there's nothing to reuse: a paused turn needs a state that is neither `running` (the unique "one running per session" index, `recover`, and Stop semantics all depend on that meaning a live task) nor an ended state. The question itself isn't a new kind of row: the call that asked is the turn's last kept message, and the answer becomes its result. The column only holds the cards.
- **Called beside other tools → refused, not paused.** Claude needs every tool result for a reply in the next user message. Pausing mid-batch would mean holding half-built results somewhere outside the append-only record, so the model is told to ask on its own instead. That costs one extra round trip in a case the system prompt and the tool description both tell it to avoid.
- **The answer reaches the model as `The person answered: <text>`**, whether it came from an option or free text. The model can see whether it matches an option.
- **No new event type.** The question reaches the browser on the existing `chat_turn` event (state `asking`, `questions`), the same event that already carries every state change of a turn.

## Gates

`make gates` is green on the rebased head `8dc75d9` (on `df56804`): format, size, scripts, clippy, docs, test (native Postgres), deny, deploy, web. **app: not run**: this branch changes nothing under `app/`.
**Mutation signal:** not applicable. `crates/server` is outside `examine_globs` in `.cargo/mutants.toml`, so `cargo mutants --in-diff` over the new files reports no mutants.

## For a human, later (not a merge hold)

- [ ] In the browser, with a real model: ask for an edit with a real taste fork (for example, music shorter than the video). Check that the card appears, that one click resumes the same turn, that typing in the composer instead also resumes it, and that Stop clears the card.
- [ ] Check the card looks right next to the quote box, in light and dark themes.
- [ ] Watch whether Gemini 3.8 Flash and Claude ask *sparingly* in practice. The system prompt line is the lever if either asks too much.

title: Web library: download any of your files (#711)
body:
## What changed

**Server** (`crates/server/src/http/library.rs`, new `http/disposition.rs`)
- `GET /api/library/{id}/file?download=1` sends the same bytes (still in ranges, so resumable downloads work) with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="…"; filename*=UTF-8''…`.
- Saved under the file's **name with its real extension**: the extension is added unless the name already ends in it, case-insensitively (an upload is usually `clip.mp4`; a generation `Narration` becomes `Narration.mp3`; `Rag.MID` stays `Rag.MID`).
- The header is safe whatever the user named the file: `filename=` is an ASCII stand-in with no `"`, `\` or control characters; `filename*=` is RFC 8187 percent-encoding (only `attr-char`s pass through), so accents and emoji survive exactly. `/`, `\` and control characters are replaced in both. If the header ever failed to build, the response falls back to a bare `attachment` rather than failing the download.
- `docs/web.md` and the route table in `http/mod.rs` describe the flag.

**Web** (`web/src/files/`)
- New `Download.tsx`: `DownloadAction` (small icon over a tile's corner, using #719's `actions` slot) and `DownloadButton` (labelled, in the details sheet beside Play/View/Open). Both are plain `<a href download>` links, the way a render downloads, so the browser streams large files straight to disk.
- `FileBrowser`: every tile on the library page and every tile in the editor's **Library modal** (picking mode) gets the download action. Refused tiles (MIDI, already in the project) download too: saving isn't picking. The link is outside the tile's main button and stops click/double-click propagation, so a download never selects, opens or picks.
- `api.library.downloadUrl(id)`.

## Why

#711: every file the user owns, paid generations included, can leave the web app. This also makes `synth_export`'s reply ("Kept in your library … where you can download it", #716) true for `.mid` files, which have no thumbnail and download like any other kind.

## Per-user isolation

`file` loads the row through `state.library.get(member.user, id)`, which is scoped to the caller, and builds the disk path from the caller's id. So another user's id is a 404 before anything is opened. Tested:
- `tests/library/download.rs`: the owner gets the bytes and the header (including after a rename to a non-ASCII name with quotes); without the flag there's no `Content-Disposition`; another user gets **404** with no header.
- `tests/library/files.rs`'s isolation loop now also covers `?download=1`.
- Unit tests in `disposition.rs` for extension handling, path characters and the exact header.
- `web/src/files/download.test.tsx`: every tile has a download link on the page and in picking mode (refused tiles included), never nested inside the tile's `<button>`, pointing at `?download=1`.

## Decisions

- **`?download=1` rather than a sibling route.** It's the same file under the same ownership rule, and only one header changes. Keeping it in one handler means the download can't drift from the playback route's scoping. The URL is different from the playing one, so the `immutable` browser cache never hands one back for the other.
- The flag counts as set if present (`?download` with any value), so a client doesn't trip over `=true` vs `=1`.
- I didn't touch `http/renders.rs`'s own simpler `filename=` (render names are reduced to `[A-Za-z0-9 _-]`, which is safe already). It's in #698's area; moving it onto `disposition::attachment` can be a later tidy-up.
- I didn't add a download button to the Viewer: the details sheet that opens it already has one.

## Gates

`make gates` on this branch, rebased on `41fd202`: **all green**: format, size, scripts, clippy, docs, test (3226 passed, Postgres 16 native), deny, deploy, web. The app gate was skipped because nothing under `app/` changed. No mutation run: `crates/server` isn't in `.cargo/mutants.toml`'s `examine_globs`, so `cargo mutants --in-diff` found no mutants in scope.

## Human checklist (not a hold)

- [ ] In a real browser, the download icon on a library tile opens the save dialog (or saves) with the file's name and extension. Try one upload, one generated file and one `.mid`.
- [ ] Same from the editor's Library modal: the click saves and does **not** add the file to the project.
- [ ] A file renamed with accents or emoji saves under that exact name.

Closes #711
